      • store

        public java.util.List<CloudFileOperationStatus> store(java.util.List<java.lang.String> localFilesOrDirectories,
                                                      java.lang.String localFSPrefix,
                                                      java.lang.String cloudPathPrefix,
                                                      boolean waitUntilDone)
        Stores a list of local files or directories to the secure cloud directory. The method walks local directories, maps them to cloud paths based on the provided prefixes, encrypts their contents and metadata, and uploads them.
        Parameters:
        localFilesOrDirectories - List of absolute local file or directory paths (e.g. /tmp/myfile.txt, /tmp/dir1)
        localFSPrefix - The local path prefix to be stripped before uploading
        cloudPathPrefix - The cloud path prefix to prepend to the resulting cloud file
        waitUntilDone - If true, blocks until all uploads finish. If false, returns immediately with UPLOADING status.
        Returns:
        A list of CloudFileOperationStatus tracking the state of each file

      • listCloudFilesVersions

        public java.util.Iterator<java.lang.String[]> listCloudFilesVersions(java.lang.String cloudPathPrefix,
                                                                     java.lang.Boolean includingSubdirectories,
                                                                     java.lang.String timeIntervalStart,
                                                                     java.lang.String timeIntervalEnd)
        List all files that match the cloudPathPrefix and timeInterval
        Parameters:
        cloudPathPrefix - Prefix that matches all the cloud files for this function call. For example for a file "/My Files/file1.txt" it can be "/My Fi"

        timeIntervalStart - Filter in all the files with creation time larger or equal than that value. Use null to ignore it.

      • deletePaths

        public java.util.List<CloudFileOperationStatus> deletePaths(java.lang.String[] cloudPaths,
                                                            java.lang.String timeIntervalStart,
                                                            java.lang.String timeIntervalEnd)
        Deletes an explicit list of cloud file paths in one call.

        Resolves every path with includingSubdirectories=true (so a single file path matches directly), then invokes deleteCloudFiles once on the combined CloudFile set.

        Parameters:
        cloudPaths - cloud file paths to delete (must not be null or empty)
        timeIntervalStart - Deletes versions created on or after this timestamp (optional)
        timeIntervalEnd - Deletes versions created on or before this timestamp (optional)
        Returns:
        A list of CloudFileOperationStatus detailing the operation state

      • getFileInputStream

        public java.io.InputStream getFileInputStream(java.lang.String cloudFilePath,
                                              java.lang.Long snapshotTime,
                                              java.lang.Long startPosition,
                                              int howManyChunksInParallel)
        Create and return InputStream for AltaStata file
        Parameters:
        cloudFilePath - The file path on the cloud
        snapshotTime - File versions creation time should match this snapshot or be last nearest. Use current time for default.

      • getFileInputStream

        public java.io.InputStream getFileInputStream(java.lang.String cloudFilePath,
                                              java.lang.Long snapshotTime,
                                              java.lang.Long startPosition,
                                              int howManyChunksInParallel,
                                              boolean trustCachedSize)
        Same as #getFileInputStream(String, Long, Long, Long, int) but with an opt-in trustCachedSize flag. When true, the caller declares this file's content is immutable (write-once, no appends), so the per-open fresh cloud GET of the size attribute is skipped and the cached value is trusted — a big win for read-many workloads such as ML dataset epochs. On a cold cache it still fetches size fresh, so correctness is preserved. Default (false): always re-fetch size (mutable-file safe behavior).

      • readBufferFromInputStreamAsBase64

        public java.lang.String readBufferFromInputStreamAsBase64(java.io.InputStream inputStream,
                                                          int size)
                                                   throws java.io.IOException
        Read a chunk from the InputStream and return it as a Base64-encoded String. Py4J transfers String values ~10x faster than byte[] because byte arrays are serialized element-by-element. This method lets Python stream large files chunk-by-chunk without touching the local filesystem while still avoiding slow byte[] transfers. Returns null when the stream is exhausted (0 bytes read).
        Parameters:
        inputStream - the InputStream to read from
        size - maximum number of bytes to read in this chunk
        Returns:
        Base64-encoded chunk, or null at end-of-stream
        Throws:
        java.io.IOException - on I/O error

      • getBufferAsBase64

        public java.lang.String getBufferAsBase64(java.lang.String cloudFilePath,
                                          java.lang.Long snapshotTime,
                                          java.lang.Long startPosition,
                                          int howManyChunksInParallel,
                                          int size)
                                   throws java.io.IOException
        Get file content as a Base64-encoded String. Py4J transfers String values far more efficiently than byte[] because byte arrays are serialized element-by-element in the Py4J protocol, whereas Strings use standard UTF encoding. The ~33% Base64 size overhead is far outweighed by the faster wire transfer.
        Parameters:
        cloudFilePath - cloud object path
        snapshotTime - version timestamp
        startPosition - byte offset to start reading
        howManyChunksInParallel - chunk pre-fetch window
        size - total bytes to read (-1 for entire file)
        Returns:
        Base64-encoded file content
        Throws:
        java.io.IOException - on I/O error
